controls.label: Risk free rate
controls.note: 10-year Treasury proxy; risk-free base for CAPM cost of equity across all four segments.

controls.label: Equity risk premium
controls.note: Market equity risk premium (Rm-Rf). Single highest-leverage macro input in the model -- moves all four segment WACCs at once (see Sensitivity tab). Updated 0.0500 -> 0.0445 per Damodaran's July 1, 2026 country ERP update (US-specific total ERP, "ERPs by country" tab, row 160) -- more current than the mature-market 4.23% figure cited in the initial comparison.

controls.label: Pre-tax cost of debt
controls.note: Pre-tax cost of debt; applied after-tax (x(1-LT cash tax rate)) as the debt leg of each segment's WACC.

controls.label: Space
controls.note: Lowered from 1.4 -- Space's revenue is heavily government-weighted (11 of 12 NSSL missions, all five 2025 ISS crew/cargo missions, 80%+ of global mass to orbit), and government launch demand doesn't cycle with the broader market the way commercial demand does. Traditional defense primes trade closer to 0.7-1.0; 1.00 reflects that mix without assuming Space is as insulated as a pure prime.

controls.label: Connectivity
controls.note: Lowered from 1.25 -- consistent with Connectivity's status as the most proven, most mature segment (already at the risk-premium floor). Mature subscription-revenue satellite ISPs should price closer to traditional telecom betas (0.5-0.8) than to a generic growth business; 0.90 moves in that direction without assuming full telecom-like stability given Starlink's still-early penetration.

controls.label: AI
controls.note: Lowered from 1.7, modestly -- high-growth AI/tech genuinely carries elevated systematic risk (disproportionately sensitive to rate environment and risk appetite), which is a market-wide phenomenon distinct from the segment-specific competitive risk already captured in AI's 1.5% idiosyncratic premium. Kept closest to its prior level of the four segments.

controls.label: Expansion
controls.note: Lowered from 2.0 -- Expansion is a convex, option-like payoff, and options don't have a stable beta (it rises further from the strike, falls deeper past it); a single static beta is a known simplification, not a precise estimate. Still the highest of the four, reflecting the segment's undefined, unsourced economics.

controls.label: Space
controls.note: Idiosyncratic risk premium added on top of CAPM cost of equity (e.g. execution or company-specific risk). Lowered 1.0% -> 0.0% -- Space has earned a genuine track-record discount (670+ launches, 80%+ of 2025 global mass to orbit, proven reusability) and benefits from the platform's financing backstop; now at the pure CAPM floor, same as Connectivity.

controls.label: Connectivity
controls.note: 0 reflects Connectivity's status as the most mature, proven cash-generative segment.

controls.label: AI
controls.note: 0 -- contract-backed revenue from Anthropic/Google/Reflection reduces idiosyncratic risk relative to Expansion. Raised 0.0% -> 1.5% -- applying the track-record logic rigorously cuts both ways: AI is the least-proven of the three real segments, competing against better-funded, more established labs with no comparable demonstrated moat. Zero premium was too generous once judged on AI's own merits rather than the company's track record broadly.

controls.label: Expansion
controls.note: Raised from 1% to 5% to better reflect Expansion's convex/option-like payoff, which a flat WACC discount doesn't fully capture on its own. 3rd-largest single lever in the model -- see Sensitivity tab.

controls.label: Total cluster target
controls.note: Raised base case from 2,000MW to 3,600MW, and slider max from 2,000MW to 5,000MW -- research (July 2026) found Colossus had already reached ~2,000MW as of Jan 2026 (555,000 GPUs), so the prior ceiling implied zero further growth, contradicting xAI's own stated 1M-GPU target (~3,600MW at current density). 5,000MW slider max leaves headroom above that stated target.

controls.label: Price per MW ($M)
controls.note: Merchant price for uncontracted AI capacity ($M/MW/year); also the rate at which expired contracted capacity (e.g. Grok, and Anthropic/Google/Reflection post-term) is repriced. Caution: at the lowest settings, the same dynamic as the margin ramp speed input can occur -- suppressed revenue combined with slow margin recovery can drive AI's own EV negative at the extreme low end.

controls.note: Annual price appreciation applied to the merchant price.

controls.label: Margin ramp speed
controls.note: Convergence speed toward target margin. Raw Min=0.0 produces a degenerate -$179/share outlier (AI margin never recovers from its deeply negative 2025 base). Swing below uses a representative low bound of 0.2 instead. Caution: at the slowest settings, AI stays unprofitable long enough into the forecast that cumulative losses can outweigh the segment's terminal value, driving AI's own EV negative (verified, not a formula error -- a genuine consequence of scaling revenue while remaining unprofitable for years).

controls.label: Contract termination risk (Anthropic/Google)
controls.note: Applies once 90-day termination rights are active, 2027 onward. Expected-value haircut on Anthropic/Google contracted revenue and MW once termination rights are active (Anthropic early 2027, Google 1/1/27). Freed MW reverts to merchant/uncontracted demand at the market price, same mechanism as the Grok exclusion (Operating sheet AI revenue formula). 0% = full contractual term realized; 50% = severe churn risk.

controls.label: Space
controls.note: R&D-proportional catalyst weight for Space in the platform-maturity composite. Rounded from the FY25 R&D split ($3,004M of $8,643M total, ~34.8%; see 424B4). Direct input -- Connectivity (row 125) is the calculated residual, guaranteeing all three sum to 100%.

controls.label: Connectivity
controls.note: Calculated as 1 - Space - AI, guaranteeing the three weights always sum to 100%. FY25 R&D was $575M of $8,643M total (~6.7%; see 424B4) -- Connectivity is the mature cash engine, not where R&D dollars are being spent, consistent with carrying the smallest and residual weight.

controls.label: AI
controls.note: R&D-proportional catalyst weight for AI. Rounded from the FY25 R&D split ($5,064M of $8,643M total, ~58.6%; see 424B4). Highest weight -- most of the company's R&D is going toward AI, consistent with it being the primary Expansion catalyst. Direct input, paired with Space as the two levers a user sets; Connectivity (row 125) absorbs the residual.

controls.label: Readiness to start (strike)
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Strike (weighted platform maturity)." Weighted platform maturity (composite) threshold below which Expansion revenue is exactly zero -- the 'strike price' of the option-like payoff.

controls.label: Speed once started (convexity)
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Convexity exponent." Convexity/shape exponent. 1.0 = linear (no optionality); 2.0 = moderate convexity (current); 3.0+ = aggressive, back-loaded payoff. Revenue always reaches $100,000M (the current Ultimate Size input, row 153) by 2035 regardless of this setting -- convexity only reshapes the path, not the destination.

controls.label: Revenue scale - calculated
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Revenue scale (at full maturity, composite=1)." Live: single ultimate-size input (row 153, currently $100,000M) / (2035 composite - strike)^convexity. Auto-recalculates as strike, convexity, or the size input change.

controls.label: Depreciation rate
controls.note: Annual depreciation as % of beginning PP&E.

controls.label: Capital efficiency
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Capital efficiency ($ revenue growth per $1 growth capex; lighter than Space/Connectivity, reflecting reuse of existing platform infrastructure)." $ of revenue growth per $1 of growth capex. Deliberately lighter than Space/Connectivity, reflecting reuse of existing platform infrastructure rather than building new dedicated capacity.

controls.label: Maintenance capex
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Maintenance capex (% of prior-year revenue)." Maintenance capex as % of prior-year Expansion revenue.

controls.label: Bear/bull range (spread)
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Scenario spread (Bear = 1-spread, Bull = 1+spread; Base = 1, fixed):." Single input replaces separate Bear/Base/Bull composite multipliers. Current calibration (30%) was already symmetric, so this is a pure structural simplification -- zero change to today's numbers.

controls.label: Odds of bear/bull (probability)
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Tail probability (Bear = Bull = this value; Base = 1 - 2x, fixed):." Single input replaces separate Bear/Base/Bull probabilities -- also structurally guarantees the three probabilities sum to 100%, which the prior three-input version relied on the user to maintain manually.

controls.label: Bull-case upside boost
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Bull scenario scale multiplier (applied only to Bull revenue -- represents genuinely new, currently-unmodeled opportunity beyond the base $625,000M ceiling, not just faster realization of it)." Recommended: 2.0x. Modest and defensible -- a genuine "platform surprises to the upside" case, not a lottery ticket. For context: AI's own TAM claim in the roadshow jumped ~7x ($3.8T to $26.5T) after the xAI acquisition -- a real precedent for large re-ratings, but for an already-massive, established segment, not a currently-undefined bucket like Expansion. 2.0x does not flip the convexity-value relationship (that needs ~6-8x); it's offered as an honest, independently-defensible number, not one chosen to force a particular conclusion.

controls.label: Market potential
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Ultimate size ($M)." Single input, not TAM x share -- multiplying two unknowns for a currently-undefined business didn't add real rigor, just an extra input. No hard constraint: the prior Data Validation was removed on the view that a user with genuine conviction Expansion exceeds simply leveraging the platform -- and given SPCX's investment horizon is plausibly measured in decades, not the model's 10-year explicit window -- shouldn't be walled off from expressing that. Wide slider range offered as guidance only.

controls.label: Starting growth - calculated
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Elevated near-term growth rate (gS) -- live, = Expansion's own 2034->2035 growth." Not a separate judgment call -- pulled directly from the model's own observed momentum in the last explicit-forecast year.

controls.label: Years to mature
controls.note: Formerly labeled: "Fade period, N (years to reach the long-run rate)." 17.5 years = midpoint of a 15-20 year range, anchored to AWS's real-world maturation timeline (launch to mature-growth-rate status) as the closest "leverages an existing platform" analog available.
